subject: physics
question_text: State and explain the first law of thermodynamics.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 12 (Thermodynamics) Short Answer Question 1 (printed p.126). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW is the first law, with Q positive for heat supplied to the system and negative for heat leaving it, W positive for work done by the system and negative for work done on it; the law is the statement of conservation of energy for a system exchanging heat and work with its surroundings.

steps.label: The statement
lines: When heat is given to a system, part
of it raises the internal energy of
the system and the rest goes into
external work done by the system.
steps.margin_note: State the law in one sentence: heat given to a system raises its internal energy and does external work, together.
steps.why: This sentence is the whole law in words; every other part of the answer only writes it in symbols and explains the symbols.
common_mistakes: Saying heat becomes only internal energy or only work. The law splits it between both.
Writing the equation only, with no sentence. The question asks to state AND explain.
steps.memory_tip: Heat splits two ways: part raises internal energy, part becomes work.

steps.label: The equation
lines: In symbols, for a small change,
ΔQ is the heat supplied, ΔU is the
change in internal energy and ΔW is
the external work done by the system.
steps.margin_note: Define ΔQ, ΔU and ΔW right after writing the equation.
steps.why: Writing the equation without naming the three quantities leaves the symbols undefined, and the definitions are worth their own mark.
common_mistakes: Writing the equation with no symbol defined. All three symbols need a name.
Mixing up ΔU and ΔW — ΔU is internal energy, ΔW is work, not the other way round.
steps.memory_tip: Q splits as U plus W: heat in equals energy stored plus work out.

steps.label: What the law means
lines: The first law is the law of
conservation of energy, applied to a
system exchanging heat and work with
steps.margin_note: Name it explicitly as conservation of energy — this is the mark for saying WHY the law holds.
steps.why: The equation alone is a bookkeeping relation; naming it as energy conservation is what makes it a LAW and not just an algebraic identity.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the words 'conservation of energy' — the connection is the point of this mark, not implied by the equation alone.
Saying energy can be created if enough work is done. The law forbids that in every case.
steps.memory_tip: First law = energy conservation, written for heat and work.

steps.label: The sign convention
lines: The equation needs a fixed sign

lines.text: W > 0 for work done by the system
W < 0 for work done on the system

steps.margin_note: Give both signs for Q and both for W — one direction each is not enough.
steps.why: The same equation gives a different answer depending on which way heat and work are taken as positive, so the convention has to be stated, not assumed.
common_mistakes: Giving only the positive case for Q or W and leaving the negative case unstated.
Reversing the convention — calling work done ON the system positive. The standard convention here takes work done BY the system as positive.
steps.memory_tip: Heat IN is positive; work done BY the system is positive.

insider_note: The sign convention is the mark most often left out — write both signs for Q and both for W, not just one.
